claims.text: The initial PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution nanoparticles are 3–10 nm in size.
The as-synthesized nanoparticles have a uniform elemental distribution.
Short reductive annealing in H2 at approximately 200–250 °C will cause slight Pd enrichment at the nanoparticle surface.
Near-surface Pd enrichment alters the local lattice strain.
Near-surface Pd enrichment shifts the d-band center.
The strain and d-band changes caused by Pd enrichment make adsorption and activation of ethanol-oxidation intermediates more favorable.
More favorable adsorption and activation of ethanol-oxidation intermediates lowers the ethanol-oxidation onset potential.
More favorable adsorption and activation of ethanol-oxidation intermediates increases current density.
The Pd-enriched catalyst will have a lower onset potential than the homogeneous PtPdRhRuIrOs baseline.
The Pd-enriched catalyst will have a higher steady-state ethanol-oxidation current than the homogeneous baseline.
The proposed mechanism should hold for 3–10 nm particles in acidic aqueous electrolyte, such as 0.5 M H2SO4, at approximately 70 °C.
Significant changes in particle size, pH, or operating temperature may cause deviations from the proposed mechanism.
Excessive segregation or deactivation during long-term cycling could reduce the anticipated performance improvement.
